newsitem.title: GERMANY: D. Babcock first-half sales rise.
newsitem.headline: D. Babcock first-half sales rise.

text.p: German engineering group Deutsche Babcock AG said on Monday sales in the first half of 1996/97 rose 12 percent to 3.3 billion marks while orders rose one percent to 4.1 billion marks.

For the full year the company said it expected sales to rise 600 million marks to 9.3 billion marks. It also expected a loss of about half of the 444 million mark setback from from the previous year, the company said in a statement.
Babcock, which was forced into an emergency reorganisation after last year's loss, said it expected orders for the full year to rise about 12 percent to 9.3 billion marks.
As of March 31, the number of employees was down 12 percent to 29,222. It expected the total to fall to 28,800 by September 31, the close of the 1996/97 business year.

The restructuring was showing results in its machinery and tubing units. The plan calls for Babcock to shed non-core businesses and reduce the number of companies in which holds shares to about 100. It had stakes in more than 260 businesses last year.
BDAG Balcke-Duerr AG, a consutrction engineering firm in which Babcock holds a 67 percent stake, last week said strong sales an order growth would allow it to break even in 1996/97.
